sections.title: What is a Surface Form?
sections.content: A surface form is an inflected, conjugated, or otherwise modified version of a lemma. While the lemma is the base dictionary form (e.g., 'धावणे' / to run), surface forms represent how the word actually appears in use (e.g., 'धावली' / she ran, 'धावतो' / he runs). Surface forms connect to specific grammatical features like gender, number, person, and politeness.

fields.name: Latin Transliteration
fields.description: Optional transliteration using Latin characters. Helps with pronunciation and searchability.
fields.guidance: Use standard transliteration schemes (e.g., ISO 15919 or simplified IAST). If the lemma already has transliteration, follow a similar pattern for consistency.

fields.name: Notes
fields.description: Internal editorial notes. These are for creators and curators only—they are not shown to learners.
fields.guidance: Use notes to record editorial decisions, regional variations, or context. Examples: "Used in Mumbai dialect", "Archaic form", "Cross-reference with X lemma".
fields.purpose: This field is purely for internal documentation and workflow management.

items.mistake: Using lemma form as surface form
items.solution: Surface forms should be inflected/conjugated. Use the actual form as it appears in text (e.g., 'धावली' for past tense, 'धावतो' for present tense).

items.example: Creating a verb surface form but selecting 'noun' as form type
items.solution: Form type must match the grammatical category. Verb inflections → verb type, noun variations → noun type.
Check if a similar surface form already exists. Each unique combination of form text and features should exist only once.
